Answer: B
Reason: The images show a right-sided pleural effusion with associated compressive atelectasis of the right lower lobe. In the context of an 82-year-old female presenting with dyspnea and these specific radiological findings (often accompanied by dextroposition or other anomalies in such case reports), this constellation is characteristic of Scimitar syndrome (congenital pulmonary venolobar syndrome), where anomalous venous drainage leads to hypoplasia and recurrent issues like effusions/infections that can present late in life.
